findings.rationale: The materialization name is derived only from the source stem and process ID. Repeated or concurrent calls for the same Markdown file in one process therefore share a pathname: each write can truncate the other's file and either guard can remove it while still in use. Because std::fs::write follows an existing symlink and Drop removes the pathname unconditionally, a pre-existing or replaced entry can also redirect the write or make cleanup affect a file this state did not uniquely create.

The general verifier rejects unsupported --deadlock values, but the specialized parser accepts any string and passes it onward. Specialized commands can consequently violate the verifier's documented warn/error/ignore contract and defer malformed input to downstream code.
